paragraphs: The XJR has been part of the XJ range since 1994, and across its four generations has used three different supercharged engines — from the AJ16 inline‑six through to the AJ133S V8. The full breakdown by engine code is below. *The XJR is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.* Jaguar XJR Engine Codes AJ16 (X300) A 4.0‑litre supercharged inline‑six fitted to the XJR from 1994 to 1997 (X300 generation). This was the last of the classic Jaguar six‑cylinder engines before the switch to V8s. No specific known issue pattern is independently confirmed for this application, but we rebuild it to the same standard as our other XJR engines. Check Your AJ16 XJR → [link to quote form] AJ‑V8 Supercharged (X308 / X350) A 4.0‑litre (X308, 1997–2003) or 4.2‑litre (X350, 2002–2009) supercharged V8. This family powered the XJR through two generations and is generally robust, though we always inspect timing chain components and gaskets during a rebuild. Check Your AJ‑V8 XJR → [link to quote form] AJ133S (X351) The 5.0‑litre supercharged V8 fitted to the XJR from 2009 to 2019. Known for the timing chain tensioner and guide design flaw, plus water pump bearing/seal failure (see the callout above). We replace the timing chain, tensioners, guides and water pump as standard on every AJ133S rebuild. Check Your AJ133S XJR → [link to quote form] Jaguar XJR Engine Compatibility Because the XJR spans three distinct supercharged engines across four generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an earlier engine's parts will work on a later car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact engine code (AJ16, AJ‑V8 or AJ133S) via registration or VIN - Your generation (X300, X308, X350 or X351) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic XJR quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car. Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required — submit your registration for a fixed‑price quote within 30 minutes. Related Jaguar XJ Variants Looking for a different XJ engine? We also cover: [Jaguar XJ6 Engine →] · [Jaguar XJ8 Engine →] · [Jaguar XJ 3.0d Engine →] · [Jaguar XJ 3.0 V6 Supercharged Engine →] · [Jaguar XJ 5.0 V8 Engine →] · [Jaguar XJ Super V8 Engine →] [← View All Jaguar XJ Engines] Frequently Asked Questions What engine does the Jaguar XJR use? It depends on the generation. The X300 (1994‑1997) uses the AJ16 4.0‑litre supercharged inline‑six. The X308 (1997‑2003) uses a 4.0‑litre supercharged V8 (AJ‑V8). The X350 (2002‑2009) uses a 4.2‑litre supercharged V8 (AJ‑V8). The X351 (2009‑2019) uses the 5.0‑litre supercharged V8 (AJ133S). Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your car has. How much does a Jaguar XJR engine rebuild cost? Rebuilds for the supercharged V8 models start from £5,500. Pricing for the early AJ16 is confirmed on registration — submit your reg for a fixed‑price quote. Which engine code is fitted to my XJR? Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the AJ16, AJ‑V8 or AJ133S before you're quoted anything. Do you rebuild AJ133S XJR engines? Yes. We replace the timing chain, tensioners, guides and water pump as standard on every AJ133S rebuild. Do you rebuild AJ‑V8 supercharged XJR engines? Yes. We inspect and replace worn components as part of the rebuild, though this engine family does not share the AJ133S timing chain design flaw. Do you rebuild AJ16 XJR engines? Yes. We rebuild the early supercharged six‑cylinder to the same standard as our V8 work. Do you supply used XJR engines? Yes, in some cases a matched low‑mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation. Can you recover my XJR if the engine has failed? Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking. How long does an XJR engine rebuild take? Most rebuilds are completed within 3‑5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop. Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine? For most XJR owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12‑month unlimited‑mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the XJR from 2023 to present. The engine features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older engine V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every engine rebuild.
